title: In situ characterization of a photon-subtraction device via heralding counts and homodyne detection
authors: Priyanka Sharma, Matteo G. A. Paris, Stefano Olivares
abstract: Photon subtraction is one of the most important techniques for generating non-Gaussian optical states and constitutes a key resource for quantum information processing and quantum metrology. The practical performance of a photon-subtraction device is primarily determined by the transmissivity of the beam splitter and the quantum efficiency of the heralding detector. Accurate knowledge of these parameters is therefore essential for assessing the quality of the generated non-classical states. In this work, we propose an experimentally feasible in situ scheme for the simultaneous estimation of these two parameters using only the measurement data produced during the operation of the device. Our protocol combines the click statistics of an on/off heralding detector with homodyne measurements performed on the transmitted mode of the beam splitter when fed by a displaced squeezed state. Within the framework of classical multi-parameter estimation theory, we derive the corresponding Fisher information matrix and investigate both joint and sequential estimation strategies. For simultaneous measurement of parameters, we evaluate the sloppiness of the underlying statistical model and analyze its dependence on the measured quadrature, probe photon number, squeezing fraction, beam splitter transmissivity, and detector efficiency. Our analysis proves that an appropriate choice of the homodyne quadrature substantially reduces parameter degeneracy and enables efficient simultaneous estimation. Furthermore, we show that the joint estimation strategy consistently provides a lower estimation bound than the sequential estimation approach over a broad range of experimentally relevant parameters.
summary: This paper proposes a novel, in situ method to simultaneously characterize the key imperfections ($	au$ and $\eta$) of a photon-subtraction device using only its operational measurement data. By applying multi-parameter estimation theory, the authors prove that a joint estimation strategy is statistically superior to sequential methods for accurately determining these critical device parameters.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for an experimentally feasible method to simultaneously estimate the transmissivity ($	au$) of a beam splitter and the quantum efficiency ($\eta$) of a heralding detector in a photon-subtraction device.
main_result: The joint estimation strategy using combined homodyne and click statistics provides a lower estimation bound than sequential estimation, proving it is the superior method for characterizing the device parameters.
method: The authors employ classical multi-parameter estimation theory, deriving the total Fisher information matrix by combining contributions from detector click statistics and conditional homodyne measurements.
model_or_system: The system is a photon-subtraction device where a displaced squeezed state interacts with vacuum at a beam splitter. The measurement involves homodyne detection on the transmitted mode and counting clicks in the reflected mode.
key_observables: Detector click statistics, homodyne measurement results (quadrature distribution), and the Fisher information matrix.
important_parameters: Beam splitter transmissivity ($	au$), detector quantum efficiency ($\eta$), squeezing fraction ($ eta$), and mean photon number ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the output state remains Gaussian due to the linear mode transformation, and it compares the joint estimation bound against the sequential estimation bound.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of the sloppiness parameter ($S$) on the homodyne phase ($\phi$), the comparison of estimation bounds between joint and sequential methods, and the effect of squeezing ($ eta$) on the estimation uncertainty.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem and the measurement setup. It then develops the theoretical framework using Fisher information for both 'on' and 'off' detection events. The core of the work compares the statistical performance of joint vs. sequential estimation strategies, concluding with analyses on parameter dependence (e.g., on squeezing or photon number).
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical tools (Fisher information, sloppiness) to assess the practical limitations and optimal measurement protocols for quantum state generation resources, which is crucial for advancing quantum information processing.
